channel.title: [podly] The AI Daily Brief: Artificial Intelligence News and Analysis
channel.description: A daily news analysis show on all things artificial intelligence. NLW looks at AI from multiple angles, from the explosion of creativity brought on by new tools like Midjourney and ChatGPT to the potential disruptions to work and industries as we know them to the great philosophical, ethical and practical questions of advanced general intelligence, alignment and x-risk.

item.title: Why You Should Try Gemini Neon (Even if You Love Fable)
item.ns0:encoded:
Google’s Gemini Neon edged out Fable on a coding benchmark, but its best pitch may be as a second opinion. NLW shares how Neon helped him find the story in an oil episode that Claude and ChatGPT kept turning into a Wikipedia entry, and what happened when he pushed back on its ideas. In the headlines: Anthropic closes its first day of trading up 17%, and Chinese AI labs warn that new U.S. chip restrictions could delay model releases.

item.title: Why the AI Kids Hate Astra 6.2
item.ns0:encoded:
Early testers say OpenAI’s Astra 6.2 stops halfway through coding projects and cuts its writing so short it’s hard to follow. But with the cost per task down 35% on one benchmark, is OpenAI betting that helping millions of office workers get through their busywork matters more than winning over developers? In the headlines: Nvidia’s board says it won’t reinstate Jensen Huang, and a wave of outages raises questions about the rush to modernize aging systems.

item.title: How Business AI Use is Changing
item.ns0:encoded:
In October, businesses tracked by Ramp used 36% more AI tokens while spending just 2% more. Data from Ramp, Databricks, and Arcana show companies switching models and expanding AI use beyond coding, while autonomous agent adoption lags. In the headlines: the push to bring Jensen Huang back to Nvidia, new U.S. chip export controls, and OpenAI’s limits on independent safety evaluators.

item.title: 5 Questions That Could Reshape AI
item.ns0:encoded:
Anthropic’s IPO could change how Wall Street judges the entire AI industry, while the fight over Jensen Huang’s future could reshape its most important chipmaker. NLW breaks down five questions defining the week: how Anthropic’s debut will land, whether OpenAI will release a new model, whether Huang can return to Nvidia, how far the political fallout will spread, and whether Congress will tighten chip export controls.

item.title: 7 Things AI-Native Companies Do Differently
item.ns0:encoded:
What do AI-native companies actually do differently? Drawing on examples from Stripe, Shopify, Uber, Ramp, and others, NLW breaks down seven practices that turn agents into useful systems—from shared company context and automatically triggered work to verification and human accountability. Plus, why the “AI teammate” model may be giving way to something more effective: flexible groups of agents organized around the work, rather than a fixed roster of digital coworkers.

item.title: Washington Is Taking Control of AI
item.ns0:encoded:
Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia is becoming a turning point in Washington’s battle over AI and China. NLW examines how the fallout is empowering China hawks, accelerating chip export restrictions, and raising questions that go well beyond the disputed spy allegations. Plus, the competing arguments over selling chips to China—and what new leadership at Nvidia could mean for the financing that keeps the AI boom moving.
